title: Earth and Space (KS2)
subject: Science
strapline: The Solar System, day and night, and the seasons.
facts: Our Solar System has the Sun at the centre and eight planets orbiting it.
The order from the Sun: Mercury, Venus, Earth, Mars, Jupiter, Saturn, Uranus, Neptune.
The Sun, Earth and Moon are approximately spherical (ball-shaped).
The Earth spins on its axis once every 24 hours — this gives us day and night.
It is day on the side of Earth facing the Sun and night on the side facing away.
The Earth orbits the Sun once every year (about 365¼ days).
The Moon orbits the Earth about once every 28 days.

quick_quiz.q: How long does the Earth take to spin once on its axis?
Which planet is closest to the Sun?

quick_quiz.a: the Earth spinning on its axis

teacher_tips: Model day/night with a torch and a globe — the spin, not the Sun, moves.
Use a mnemonic for planet order but check they know it is distance from the Sun.
Correct "the Sun goes round the Earth" directly and early.
